# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Fiorina 161 for new arrivals, staff and inmates alike, as far as the Herald's archive can tell it.[/italic]
## The Hull Fiorina 161 is a prison under one sealed hull on the far edge of the Neroid Sector. There is no outside to walk in. The windows show black, the air comes out of the scrubbers at seventeen degrees, and the floor stays under your feet because the gravity generator keeps it there. The lights never go out. The warden calls that security. The inmates call it something else.
## The Company's Prison Weyland-Yutani owns and operates Fiorina as a [bold]maximum security prison[/bold] for the most dangerous criminals in the system. The distance is the real wall. Everything that comes in or goes out passes through Dock A or Dock B, and nothing moves through either without a signature from the warden's office. - Most inmates sleep in the bunk rooms and work the mess, the cargo floor and the hydroponics trays. - The four hard cells, A to D, sit beside the warden's office, with the armory and the interrogation room a short walk away. Nobody on staff will say what it takes to earn one. - Power comes from a fusion unit that the reactor contractors sign off every month, in writing, as a knock-off.
## Who Lives Here - [bold]Inmates[/bold], most of them serving terms that will outlast the facility. - [bold]Guards and Company staff[/bold] on long rotations, who arrive and leave in hypersleep. - [bold]Contractors[/bold] who keep the reactor, the scrubbers and the relay running, and who leave on the first transport out.
## The Dead Fiorina does not ship its dead home. The medical bay keeps a morgue and a crematorium, and the families learn of a death months late, as a line on a transfer manifest, with nothing to bury.
## The Press The Herald's Fiorina edition began in 2180 because of that line. We print the names of the dead, whoever they belonged to, and once a year we read them out at the memorial by the garden.
